newsitem.title: USA: Lyondell-Citgo Texas refinery reports gas release.
newsitem.headline: Lyondell-Citgo Texas refinery reports gas release.

text.p: A plume of noxious gas was released from Lyondell-Citgo Refining Co's 265,000 barrel per day Houston refinery on Tuesday, a refinery spokesman said.
Information was not immediately available on the process units involved in the release of sulphur dioxide or the impact of the upset on plant operations.

"As a precautionary measure, schools in the Galena Park school district downwind were advised to shelter-in-place for a brief period," the spokesman said, referring to a local practice of keeping students inside classrooms until a potential emergency is over.

Sources said the refiner on Friday planned to restart a 100,000 barrel per day crude unit taken down in late December for unplanned maintenance and was operating a 96,000 barrel per day fluid catalytic cracker at 80,000 barrels per day.
Citgo was an active buyer in the Gulf Coast and Group Three spot markets on the day, traders said.
The Houston refinery is operated under a joint venture between Lyondell Petrochemical Co and Citgo, a domestic unit of Petroleos de Venezuela SA.
